axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Supabase platform capabilities
(projects, database queries, migrations, logs, docs retrieval) as tools for coding agents.
axes.runtime:
Two forms: local npx process (stdio) + an official hosted remote line; GitHub 2,966★,
last push 2026-10-21 (GitHub API verified).
axes.local_files:
In the local form it does not directly read or write your local project files (that is the filesystem server's job) —
it operates on Supabase cloud projects: tables, migrations, logs.
axes.background: Local stdio lives and dies with the client; the hosted remote form lives on Supabase's side. No background-task semantics.
axes.tools:
Database queries/migrations, project management, logs and diagnostics, docs retrieval, etc.;
tools can be trimmed on demand (the official side supports selectively enabling tool groups); the complete inventory follows the repo README.
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives in the Supabase project itself (schema, data).
axes.permissions:
**Credential = Supabase access token, a large permission surface**: it can reach project-level APIs (including the SQL execution surface).
The official side offers tool trimming and read-only tool distinctions, but SQL write/DDL capabilities genuinely exist —
before hooking up an agent, defend on the worst-case assumption "you gave it a credential that can modify the database".
axes.fit:
Fits: coding agents directly managing your own Supabase projects (inspect schema, run migrations, read logs).
Not a fit: hard boundaries needing "read-only insurance" (trimming narrows but is not a sandbox); non-Supabase-stack projects.

mcp.transport:
Local **stdio** (npx starting a process) is primary; the official side also has a hosted remote endpoint line (details follow the official docs, not verified item by item).
Verified: repo README and GitHub API (2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
Supabase access token (scopes configurable); the local form passes the token via env var/parameter.
The official docs give guidance on token rotation and least-privilege practices — details not verified item by item.
mcp.scope:
Project level: read schema, execute SQL (including writes/DDL), manage migrations, read logs.
Tool-group trimming can shrink the exposure surface; no official docs for a tool-level human approval mechanism.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The current status and differences of the hosted remote endpoint (not verified item by item)
- The complete tool-group trimming matrix (not enumerated item by item)
- Token scope granularity details (not verified item by item)
related: A "two-forms + tool-trimming" design contrast: GitHub has a mandatory read-only switch, Supabase has no equivalent switch.
